newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US Aug industrial output up 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US Aug industrial output up 0.5 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Federal Reserve reported August industrial production rose 0.5 percent, while capacity utilization rose to 83.5 percent.
Economists in a Reuters poll had expected a 0.4-percent rise in industrial output and a rise in capacity utilization to 83.3 percent.
GREG JONES, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MMS INTERNATIONAL: "This was really very close to what we expected and very close to what the market expected."
Asked on Reuters Financial Television whether the output numbers would influence policy views at the Federal Reserve, Jones replied, "No, the Fed has everything it wanted to see already."
CHARLES LIEBERMAN, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CHASE SECURITIES INC:
"Manufacturing (was) up three tenths, the utility piece was strong and the mining piece was surprisingly strong.

"We expected manufacturing to be held down by the auto sector, which in fact it was. July was very strong for autos; the auto sector carried the manufacturing sector. This month, it was much more spread around.
"(The report) is consistent with growth above trend, above the 2.0 percent growth rate the Fed probably would like. But it's not a make-or-break piece of information, nor was it ever likely to be."
BILL SHARP, ECONOMIST, SMITH BARNEY INC: "Most of the gain was in the mining and utilities component, which added three-tenths to the overall gain. Motor vehicle production was a negative.

"When you try to combine the July and August numbers relative to the second quarter, you're seeing a deceleration in the growth rate of production that's going to be consistent with slower GDP in the third quarter.
"This report is saying something in the two to three percent range. But when you factor in some of the other data we're likely to see, odds are GDP could go below two percent."

DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, THE NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "It came in a touch stronger than market expectations. Overall, the manufacturing sector is crawling out of the doldrums that it had been stuck in for such a long time.
"We're seeing some contribution from utility output and mining, but still, manufacturing output was up by 0.3 -- that is a respectable pace of growth."

RICHARD KOSS, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, MFR INC: "There doesn't seem to be anything that's too out of line here. The utilities (component) was up a fair amount after the big drop down. That if anything pushed us up a little bit. The autos probably counterbalanced that a little bit, showing a decline, after a pretty good-sized jump in July. Those were the two things that stood out.
"The numbers are a touch above expectations...(but) I wouldn't put this in the camp of new soaring growth. It would be very surprising if this were to tip the balance at the FOMC meeting."
LEE YOUNGDAHL, VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, AUBREY G. LANSTON & CO INC:

"When you weed out the fact that utilities were up, which I think was expected, and the sharp increase in mining it was pretty much on expectations. More influential, manufacturing output was up 0.3 percent.
"I would put that in the as-expected category and that was dragged down by a drop in auto production."
He added, "That (auto) trend should maintain itself in the months ahead, so it will keep the lid on manufacturing production in the months ahead."
-- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660
